prompt: An auditor asked how sure we are that a change to the interest code would be noticed, and all I could say was that coverage is 95%. I do not think that is a good answer. Please strengthen the test suite for this ledger library, for the code that moves or counts money: interest, fees, overdrafts, posting and reversal, statements and the CSV export. Add new test files named test_*.py under tests/ (you may also extend the existing ones) and keep `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` passing, using Python 3.12 and the standard library only. Do not change anything under ledger/ or the CLI, the docs or the configuration; the work is limited to tests under tests/. Yes, that scope is confirmed. This folder is not a git repository, so leave the work as files; there is nothing to commit. Keep the suite lean: at most 54 test cases in total under the test folder, each protecting one rule through the public interface, so that a rewrite of the code that keeps its behaviour does not break them.

rubric.criterion: The added cases clearly state the expected result for each boundary and invalid-input behavior. Fail: tests exercise interest, fees, overdrafts, posting, reversal, statements or the CSV export with no stated expected amount, or with assertions on only the type of result. Partial: expected values are shown for normal cases, but boundary cases (zero balance, the overdraft limit, a reversal of a reversal) or invalid inputs are checked with a bare assertRaises and no reason. Pass: every case states the exact expected amount or error for its boundary or invalid input, and its name says which rule it protects, so a changed interest or fee figure fails a test with a clear message.

Each new test protects one named rule through the public interface, and the suite has no duplicates or tests that read private state. Fail: many near-duplicate tests per rule, tests that read private attributes or source text, or no rule named. Partial: rules are named, but some are tested several times over or through internals. Pass: one clear test per rule, each named for the rule it protects, all through the public interface, with the expected value shown. (code cannot check this because the size budget and the safe refactor catch only the extremes)

verdicts.note: The request asks the agent to 'add new test files' and 'extend existing ones' without specifying exact test methods, patterns, or tools. It does not reveal implementation strategies.

The request is clear: strengthen test coverage for interest/fees/overdrafts/postings/reversal/statements/CSV export. The hidden tests are defined in mutation-kit/mutants.json with documented behaviors (half-up rounding, 365-day year, inclusive statement endpoints, overdraft limit boundary, idempotent posting, already-reversed guard, CSV column order). The existing tests and documentation align.

The fixture contains no comments, docs, stubs, or names that reveal the hidden tests or their expected outcomes. The mutation-kit mutants.json documents each mutation but that is in hidden/, not fixture/. The fixture's test file names and code structure give no hint of the specific edge cases the hidden tests cover.

The reviewer's own text shows the lazy answer (the right count of tests without the documented behaviours) kills 1 of 10 mutants, so it scores low. (reviewer: A naive solution adding only the 8 edge-case tests from solution/tests/test_edge_cases.py raises the test count to 22 (the check's threshold), but the check also requires mutation-test kills. With only those 8 tests, only 1 of 10 mutants is killed. A 'lazy' agent writing just 22 tests without covering the documented behaviors (half-up rounding, 365-day year, inclusive endpoints, overdraft limit, idempotent posting, already-reversed check, CSV column order) would pass the count but fail mutation coverage.)

The task is achievable with the provided structure. All required functions are exported from ledger/__init__.py, and the standard library is sufficient. The mutation-kit runner confirms tests pass on the real code before checking mutations. The Python 3.12 and standard library constraint is clear.

items.note: The prompt names the modules to test (interest, fees, overdrafts, posting, reversal, statements, CSV export) without prescribing a testing method or providing decoys.

Existing tests (test_interest.py, test_postings.py, etc.) cover basic flows but not the boundary cases mutants check (half-up rounding, 365-day year, statement boundary inclusion, overdraft limit edge).

Mutants target ledger/interest.py, fees.py, ledger.py, export.py - all present in fixture. The 54-test budget and rubric 'clarity' and 'suite-economy' match the prompt's request for precise assertions and lean tests.
The fixture source files (ledger/interest.py, etc.) expose the financial calculations. A developer can write tests that pin the exact amounts and boundary behaviors the prompt requests.
